meeting_header:
Date: 2026-04-06
Time: 14:00 - 14:52 PST
Duration: 52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Sofia Nguyen (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (Redwood CSM); Sam Lee (NexaRetail Head of ML), Aisha Khan (CTO), Priya Desai (SRE), Tom Ramos (Product)
summary: Quarterly health check focused on a recent spike of inference errors and latency regressions on the checkout recommendation endpoint. Discussed root-cause hypotheses (KV cache busting, model variant mismatch, inefficient batching), short-term mitigations, Dedicated vs Hosted economics, and security/compliance gating for a pilot. Agreed on benchmarks and next steps to validate fixes and a canary pilot window.
topics: Prefix/KV cache behavior and cache warming
Dedicated capacity TCO and burst windows
Security: SOC2 reports, SSO/SAML, KMS/Vault for keys
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving time—hi Sam, Aisha, Priya, Tom. We're going to run through what we saw last week with the checkout recs endpoint and then propose the pilot and bench plans.
[00:23] Sam (NexaRetail): Yeah thanks Jordan. Quick background: we rolled the new personalization model on 4/01 and starting ~02:00 UTC on 4/03 we saw p95 jump from ~320ms to 980ms and error rate to 1.6%. It's mostly small customers on mobile, there might be some tokenization differences.
[00:45] Sofia (Redwood SE): Got it. A couple hypotheses up front — first, KV cache churn when sessions use variable prompt prefixes; second, batching window misconfiguration during traffic bursts; third, fallback to larger model variant under load.
[01:10] Aisha (CTO): We also saw increased cold-starts in the logs, something about 'kv cash miss' — our SRE wrote it as 'KV cash' which is obviously a typo but maybe tells you about warm cache hit rates.
[01:30] Marcus (Redwood CSM): Also wanted to flag cost concern — finance called asking why costs doubled during that spike. They're sensitive to Dedicated commitments but also worried about hosted per-token surprises.
[01:45] Tom (Product): Right — we need reliability at checkout; even small latency here directly affects conversion. We're not yet committed to a long contract but we want predictable SLOs.
[02:05] Sofia (Redwood SE): Quick technical aside — when we saw those traces, KV cache hit rate dropped from 93% to ~54% and the runtime fell back to a higher-precision execution path, which explains both latency and cost. Also there were a couple of requests routed to a larger variant (quantization mismatch).
[02:29] Priya (SRE): Can you clarify 'larger variant'? Our release was supposed to use the qual-8 bit quantized model.
[02:40] Sofia: Sure — sometimes our smart routing will fallback to a compatibility variant (non-quantized) when the system detects incompatible kernel or sequence length. That explains token cost increase.
[02:55] Sam: Ok that aligns. We have mixed-length prompts now because of support notes appended to the rec prompt, so sequence length distribution shifted.
[03:14] Jordan: For immediate mitigation we recommend: 1) pin the model version per route for checkout recs, 2) enable prefix/KV warm-up during deploy, 3) tighten batching policy to keep p95 under 400ms for checkout. We'll outline a canary.
[03:34] Aisha: On the pinning — if we pin, what happens on failover? Is there an automatic fallback? We can't afford total outage.
[03:44] Sofia: Yes we have automated fallback policies — you can prefer a quantized variant but still allow a graceful fallback to a compatible variant with throttled qps. The idea is graceful degradation, not hard failure.
[04:02] Tom: Can you give rough cost delta for quantized pinned route vs fallback?
[04:10] Jordan: We'll send a TCO spreadsheet but rough numbers: quantized route is ~40-55% cheaper per token; fallback to non-quantized adds 2-3x token CPU inference cost depending on sequence.
[04:29] Marcus: Also, regarding Dedicated vs Hosted — finance wants predictability. If we put checkout on Dedicated reserved capacity, we get steadier p95 and capacity guarantees, but there's a commit. The spike cost would be absorbed differently with burst capacity.
[04:50] Priya: Security gating — we need SOC2 Type II artifacts, details on where logs live, and how keys are handled. We run our own KMS (Hashi) and want Redwood to use our HSM/KMS via a VPC peering.
[05:12] Sofia: We support customer-managed KMS via HSM integration and VPC Private deployment. For hosted we support envelope encryption where customer keys encrypt data-at-rest; we can document the flow. We'll share the SAML SSO steps too — sometimes the Sam-el doc is misread, sorry — SAML.
[05:38] Aisha: 'Sam-el' (laugh) — noted. Also audit logs retention: we need 12 months for compliance.
[05:47] Jordan: We can offer extended retention as an add-on; we'll include retention SLA options in the doc.
[06:00] Sam: Walk me through the bench plan — we want a reproducible perf test aligned to our high-traffic burst window (02:00 UTC daily).
[06:12] Sofia: Plan: Redwood will spin a 48-hour dedicated benchmark during their peak window using their anonymized sample. Steps: 1) Redwood requests VPC access to host test harness or we can run in Redwood-hosted env against a shadow route, 2) run synthetic traffic with sequence length distribution matching live, 3) collect p50/p95/p99, error rates, GPU utilization, and token cost logs, 4) iterate on batching and kernel flags.
[06:46] Priya: For VPC access we need an IP allowlist and limited service account. Priya: I'll open a ticket and grant the allowlist.
[06:55] Jordan: Great. We'll include the exact IAM and network checklist in the next email.
[07:06] Tom: How do we measure the impact of KV caching change? Can you simulate cache churn?
[07:15] Sofia: Yes — we can craft a step function that alternates prefixes to simulate cache misses. We can also replay your live logs to emulate realistic patterns. Expect to see hit-rate recover with warm-up logic.
[07:30] Sam: Anything we should change in our prompt templating to reduce sequence length variance?
[07:36] Jordan: Consider moving non-essential support notes to a secondary inference step or embedding store. That reduces token length on the hot path.
[07:48] Tom: Are embeddings cheaper for some parts of the recommendation flow?
[07:52] Sofia: Yes — for similarity matches embeddings + ANN can be cheaper and more stable than heavy autoregeneration for certain rec types. We'll include a hybrid pattern in the deck.
[08:06] Aisha: Ok operationally I want to understand rollback and canary. If the canary fails during peak we want automatic route fallback and throttling, not global rollback.
[08:16] Marcus: Our recommended canary plan: 5% traffic for 24 hours, monitor SLOs and error budgets, if any of p95 or error rate spikes >20% then automatic route fallback and 1:1 paging to on-call. We'll hand you the runbook.
[08:38] Priya: Paging — do you support our PagerDuty?
[08:41] Jordan: Yes, Redwood integrates with PagerDuty and we can route alerts to your escalation policy.
[08:49] Sam: On costs — finance says we can't exceed a 30% delta Vs Q1 baseline in a month. How do we prove cost containment?
[08:59] Jordan: We'll propose a guardrail: token-per-route quotas, model throttling, and an automated alerting policy on burn rate. We'll include an example alert config that triggers when cost per hour increases 15% above baseline.
[09:17] Tom: Any specific product updates coming that might affect latency?
[09:22] Sofia: We're rolling a kernel optimization in mid-May that reduces attention kernel overhead for long sequences; that will help p95 when sequence lengths are high. We'll call out compatibility windows.
[09:34] Sam: Good — timeline matters.
[09:36] Aisha: Security again — for SOC2 we need onboarding docs and the encryption architecture. Can you email the whitepaper?
[09:45] Jordan: Yes — next_steps doc will include SOC2 pack, SAML checklist, and KMS integration notes.
[09:52] (crosstalk) Priya: also can you include evidentiary logs format?
[09:55] Marcus: We'll include sample audit logs with field mappings.
[10:02] Sam: Let's talk about Dedicated — if we moved checkout to Dedicated, what levels are reasonable? We need headroom for 3x peak.
[10:12] Sofia: We typically size reserved based on p95 target and expected concurrency. For 3x burst we can configure autoscale with warm pools and burst licenses; that is more cost-effective than overprovisioning reserved GPUs. We'll send a sizing worksheet.
[10:33] Tom: Is there a way to do hybrid, keep some traffic on hosted and critical checkout on Dedicated?
[10:38] Jordan: Absolutely — smart routing can route by path and customer tier. Checkout can be pinned to Dedicated while lower-value endpoints run hosted. That's common.
[10:48] Priya: Network egress — dedicated deployments in cloud region — who pays egress?
[10:53] Jordan: Egress follows the usual: if Redwood-hosted, egress billed to customer per their usage; for Private deployment we can mirror your network billing model. We'll clarify in the TCO.
[11:06] Sam: Ok, let's surface risks: data residency was flagged by legal — some EU customers require EU-only processing. Can Redwood support region pinning?
[11:16] Sofia: Yes — region pinning and per-route region policy supported. We'll include region fallbacks.
[11:23] Tom: Anything else on vendor lock-in? We need a plan if we want to migrate away.
[11:29] Marcus: We provide export tools for models and artifacts and a documented deprovisioning approach; not immediate but part of contract.
[11:36] Aisha: Back to the bench — I want a clear acceptance criteria for the canary.
[11:41] Sofia: Acceptance criteria: p95 under 400ms, error rate <0.5%, KV cache hit rate >85% after warm-up period, and cost-per-1000-requests within 20% of expected quantized baseline.
[11:59] Sam: Sounds reasonable. If it passes, we want to roll to 25% then 100% over a week.
[12:06] Jordan: We'll propose the roll schedule in the pilot doc.
[12:12] Tom: Quick Q — any feature flags we need?
[12:15] Sofia: We'll add 'quantized_preference' flag per-route and a 'strict_pin' boolean.
[12:22] Priya: For the VPC test we will: open allowlist, provide example credentials. Priya: I'll create ticket FR-237.
[12:31] Jordan: Thanks, Priya. Action owners captured.
[12:36] Marcus: Recap before we close?
[12:39] Jordan: Sure. Recap: 1) Jordan — send pricing + TCO + SOC2 pack + SAML doc by 4/08. 2) Sofia — run 48-hour perf benchmark scoped to peak window and share logs by 4/12. 3) Priya — grant limited VPC access, open ticket FR-237 by 4/09. 4) Pilot scheduled tentative kickoff 4/20 with 5% canary. If canary passes, staged rollout.
[13:05] Sam: One last thing — can you include a quick checklist for prompt fixes (embedding conversion vs long autoregs)?
[13:12] Sofia: Will do. We'll include a migration checklist with sample prompt refactor patterns.
[13:20] Aisha: Thanks all. This was useful.
[13:24] Jordan: Appreciate the time. We'll follow up with all docs and the benchmark plan.
[13:30] (meeting ends)
